translationRepairs: The Empress Dowager of Jin, new wife and subject Li, speaks: Zhang Yanze, Fu Zhuer, and others have come; we humbly received the reassuring letter from the Emperor Honored Father-in-Law.
The Empress Dowager of Jin, your daughter-in-law and subject Li, speaks: Zhang Yanze, Fu Zhuer, and others have come; we humbly received the reassuring letter from the Emperor Honored Father-in-Law.

s0042 晉室皇太后新婦李氏妾言 uses 新婦 as the daughter-in-law’s memorial self-style before 皇帝阿翁, not a newly married wife. Replacing “new wife” with “your daughter-in-law” restores that kinship without changing names, agents, or the letter of reassurance.

I recall that my late husband the emperor, when he was in Bing and Fen, met sudden peril; danger piled like eggs in a stack, urgency hung like an inverted cleaver; wit and courage alike were exhausted and each day and night hung by a thread.

I recall that my late husband the emperor, when he was in Bing and Fen, met sudden peril; danger piled like eggs in a stack, urgency like being hung upside down; wit and courage alike were exhausted and each day and night hung by a thread.

s0043 急若倒懸 is the stock image of hanging upside down in extremity. “Inverted cleaver” invents a blade; the proposed “urgency like being hung upside down” matches the Chinese and the already-correct idiomatic line.
Ten-odd days later they crossed the Liao River and reached Tied Prefecture in Bohai.
Ten-odd days later they crossed the Liao River and reached Tie Prefecture in Bohai.
s0070 至渤海國鐵州 names 鐵州. “Tied Prefecture” is a corrupt transliteration; Tie Prefecture matches 鐵 and the chapter’s prefecture style.
After another ten-odd days they crossed the Liao River and reached Tied Prefecture in the Bohai state.
After another ten-odd days they crossed the Liao River and reached Tie Prefecture in the Bohai state.
The same 鐵州 appears in the literal English as “Tied Prefecture.” Tie Prefecture is the supported reading.
In the eighth month, when Prince Yongkang came down from the heights, the dowager rode hard to Bazhou to see him and begged for land near Hanyang City to farm and herd and live by.
In the eighth month, when Prince Yongkang came down from the heights, the dowager rode hard to Bazhou to see him and begged for land near Han'er City to farm and herd and live by.
s0082 求於漢兒城側 is Han’er City, a Han settlement name (漢兒), not Hanyang (漢陽). The proposed place-name restores the source.
When the eighth month came and Prince Yongkang came down from the heights, the dowager rode in haste to Bazhou to see him and begged for land beside Hanyang City to farm and herd for a living.
When the eighth month came and Prince Yongkang came down from the heights, the dowager rode in haste to Bazhou to see him and begged for land beside Han'er City to farm and herd for a living.
The literal line repeats Hanyang for 漢兒城. Han’er City is the accurate English for that toponym.

The emperor, with the empress, palace women, eunuchs, and eastern and western attendants, all tore their hair and went barefoot, carrying the bier to the allotted land, burning the bones and burying them in a pit dug in the earth.

The emperor, with the empress, palace women, eunuchs, and eastern and western attendants, all let down their hair and went barefoot, carrying the bier to the allotted land, burning the bones and burying them in a pit dug in the earth.
s0090 皆被髮徙跣 is mourning with hair worn loose and feet bare, not tearing the hair. The proposed literal matches 被髮 and the already-correct idiomatic rendering.
Grand Consort An came from northern Dai; her lineage is unknown. Wife of Jing Ru, she bore the Deposed Emperor and was made Lady of Qin.
Grand Consort An came from northern Dai; her lineage is unknown. Wife of Jingru, she bore the Deposed Emperor and was made Lady of Qin.
s0094 為敬儒妻 is the given name Jingru, already written as one word elsewhere in the chapter. Splitting it as Jing Ru treats a Chinese given name as a Western surname plus given name.

The two paternal uncles were Wanyou and Wanyuan; the elder brother, Jingru; the younger brothers Jingwei, Jingde, Jingyin, Jingyun, Jinghui, and Chongyin; the sons Chonggui, Chongxin, Chongyi, Chongying, Chongjin, Chongrui, and Chonggao; the grandsons Yansxu and Yanbao.

The two paternal uncles were Wanyou and Wanyuan; the elder brother, Jingru; the younger brothers Jingwei, Jingde, Jingyin, Jingyun, Jinghui, and Chongyin; the sons Chonggui, Chongxin, Chongyi, Chongying, Chongjin, Chongrui, and Chonggao; the grandsons Yanxu and Yanbao.
s0121 孫曰延煦、延寶. 延煦 is Yanxu; Yansxu inserts an unsupported s and is not a reading of the Chinese.

The two paternal uncles were Wanyou and Wanyuan; the elder brother was Jingru; the younger brothers were Jingwei, Jingde, Jingyin, Jingyun, Jinghui, and Chongyin; the sons were Chonggui, Chongxin, Chongyi, Chongying, Chongjin, Chongrui, and Chonggao; the grandsons were Yansxu and Yanbao.

The two paternal uncles were Wanyou and Wanyuan; the elder brother was Jingru; the younger brothers were Jingwei, Jingde, Jingyin, Jingyun, Jinghui, and Chongyin; the sons were Chonggui, Chongxin, Chongyi, Chongying, Chongjin, Chongrui, and Chonggao; the grandsons were Yanxu and Yanbao.
The literal list has the same corrupt Yansxu for 延煦. Yanxu is the supported romanization.
After that no one knew their fate.
After that no one knew her fate.
s0116 後不知其所終 closes Empress Feng’s notice after 後隨帝北遷. 其 points to her end, not a plural fate of several people.

In the first month of Tianfu 2, Wanyou was posthumously raised from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor with the Staff, concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Preceptor.

In the first month of Tianfu 2, Wanyou was posthumously raised from former Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Minister over the Masses, concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Preceptor.

s0128 萬友自故金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒兼御史大夫、上柱國贈太師. 檢校司徒 is acting Situ (Minister over the Masses); 太師 is the posthumous Grand Preceptor. “Grand Preceptor with the Staff” both mistranslates 司徒 and collapses the promotion into a tautology. Restoring 故 as “former” is also required.

In the first month of the second Tianfu year, Wanyou was posthumously promoted from former Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor with the Staff, Concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Preceptor.

In the first month of the second Tianfu year, Wanyou was posthumously promoted from former Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Minister over the Masses, Concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Preceptor.
The literal chain makes the same 檢校司徒 error. Acting Minister over the Masses is the office held before the posthumous 太師.
Wanyuan was likewise raised from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Mentor with the Staff, concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Tutor.
Wanyuan was likewise raised from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of Works, concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Tutor.
s0129 檢校司空兼御史大夫、上柱國贈太傅. 檢校司空 is acting Minister of Works, not Grand Mentor; 太傅 is the posthumous Grand Tutor.
Wanyuan likewise was posthumously promoted from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Mentor with the Staff, Concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Tutor.
Wanyuan likewise was posthumously promoted from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of Works, Concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Tutor.
The literal English repeats “Grand Mentor with the Staff” for 檢校司空. Acting Minister of Works is the source office.

Jingru alone was first granted Grand Tutor from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor with the Staff, concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Pillar of the State—yet received no princely title.

Jingru alone was first granted Grand Tutor from former Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State—yet received no princely title.

s0139 敬儒始以故金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書左僕射兼御史大夫、上柱國贈太傅. The acting office is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; 兼御史大夫 is concurrent Grand Censor, omitted and displaced in the before text, while “Grand Preceptor with the Staff” is invented.

The people of Shaan suffered under his cruelty; he was recalled to the capital. Because his imperial uncle could not restrain him, his original followers Chief Custodian Su Yancun and Zheng Wenyun were demoted as a warning.

The people of Shaan suffered under his cruelty; he was recalled to the capital. Because he was an imperial uncle whom the emperor could not punish, his original followers Chief Custodian Su Yancun and Zheng Wenyun were demoted as a warning.

s0231 以其皇叔不能責也, after Jingyun asks after his “little nephew,” means Jingyun himself was the imperial uncle whom the emperor could not discipline. “His imperial uncle could not restrain him” invents a third-party uncle and reverses the kinship.

The people of Shaan suffered under his brutality; he was recalled to the capital. Because his imperial uncle could not hold him accountable, his original followers Chief Custodian Su Yancun and Zheng Wenyun were demoted as a warning.

The people of Shaan suffered under his brutality; he was recalled to the capital. Because he was an imperial uncle whom the emperor could not hold accountable, his original followers Chief Custodian Su Yancun and Zheng Wenyun were demoted as a warning.
The literal line makes the same kinship reversal. 皇叔 names Jingyun; the emperor could not hold that uncle accountable, so retainers were demoted instead.
In the first month of the seventh year he was additionally made Grand Tutor and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yi.
In the first month of the seventh year he was additionally made Grand Preceptor and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yi.
s0162 加贈太師，追封沂王. 太師 is Grand Preceptor, already the chapter’s rendering, distinct from 太傅 Grand Tutor in the preceding grant of 太尉 and elsewhere.
In the first month of the seventh year he was additionally granted Grand Tutor and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yi.
In the first month of the seventh year he was additionally granted Grand Preceptor and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yi.
The literal 加贈太師 is likewise Grand Preceptor, not Grand Tutor.
When Gaozu visited Bianzhou, he was made eastern capital commissioner.
When Gaozu visited Bianzhou, he was made regent of the Eastern Capital.
s0218 以為東都留守 is the Eastern Capital stay-behind/regent office when Gaozu went to Bianzhou, not a generic “commissioner.” “Regent of the Eastern Capital” is accurate, complete English for 留守 here.
When Gaozu visited Bianzhou, he was made eastern capital commissioner.
When Gaozu visited Bianzhou, he was made Eastern Capital stay-behind commissioner.
The literal should keep 留守 rather than flatten it to commissioner. Eastern Capital stay-behind commissioner matches the office title.

In the fifth month of the third year, Imperial Clan Director Shi Guangzan went with one hundred fifty beds of betrothal gifts to fetch the bride from Zaili’s house; the Fleeing Emperor feasted him in the Hall of Ten Thousand Years with gifts so lavish that ruler and subject outdid each other in excess—contemporaries called it glory.

In the fifth month of the third year, Imperial Clan Director Shi Guangzan went with one hundred fifty beds of betrothal gifts to fetch the bride from Zaili’s house; the Fleeing Emperor feasted Zaili in the Hall of Ten Thousand Years with gifts so lavish that ruler and subject outdid each other in excess—contemporaries called it glory.
s0185 出帝宴在禮萬歲殿 names Zhao Zaili as the banquet guest. Idiomatic “feasted him” after Shi Guangzan’s mission wrongly attributes the feast to the envoy; naming Zaili restores the Chinese.
